summary: Vladimir Druzhinin works in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Novosibirsk State Medical University (2003–2009) and Peoples' Friendship University of Russia (2013–2016), later serving as an assistant at Novosibirsk State Medical University (2009) and Novosibirsk State University (2015).

Linguist Vladimir Ivanov Georgiev (1908–1986) studied under Stefan Mladenov at Sofia University, earned a Ph.D. at Vienna, and studied in Berlin, Florence, and Paris. At Sofia University, he was Assistant (1931), Docent (1936), and Head of Linguistics (1945–1974).

Vladimir Ivanovich Kalyanov (1908–2001) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Leningrad Institute of History, Philosophy and Linguistics and under Barannikov and Shcherbatskoy. He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1937–1985) and Saint Petersburg State University (1938–1941).

Vladimir Minorsky (1877–1966) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. Educated at Moscow State University and the Lazarev Institute, he held posts at INALCO (1923), SOAS (Lecturer in 1932, Professor 1937–1944), and Cairo University (1948–1949).

Indologist and linguist Vladimir Nikolaevich Toporov (1928–2005) studied at Moscow State University (~1946–1951) under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson. He spent his career at the Institute of Slavic Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences as naučnyj sotrudnik (1954) and staršij naučnyj sotrudnik (1960).

Indologist and philosopher Vladimir P. Ivanov served as a senior researcher at the St. Petersburg Institute for Informatics and Automation in 1989 and was attested in 2009 as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Vladimir Svjatoslavovič Vorob’ëv-Desjatovskij (1927–1956) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov. He served as naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1951–1956) and taught Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (1955–1956).

Vladimir Tikhonov (born 1973), a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Saint Petersburg State, Moscow State, and Korea University. He lectured at Kyung Hee University (1997–2000) before becoming Associate Professor (2000) and Professor (2006) at Oslo.

Vladimír Miltner (1933–1997) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Charles University (1952–1967), earning a Ph.D., and worked as a research scholar at the Czech Academy of Sciences starting in 1967.

Tibetologist Volker Caumanns studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and earned a Ph.D. at Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Munich (2006–2012), Lumbini International Research Institute (2012–2015), and later Bern, Leipzig, and Hamburg.

Historian Volker Grabowsky (born 1959) studied at Kiel and Chiang Mai. He held posts at Passau (1990–1994), Hamburg (1994–1996; 2003–2004), the National University of Laos (1996–1999), and Münster (1999) before becoming Chair of Thai Studies at Hamburg in 2009.

Volker Zotz (born 1956) is a philosopher and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Vienna (~1975–1982) and under Anagarika Govinda, he held positions at Vienna, Otani, Ryukoku, Saarland University, and the University of Luxembourg.

Vrajavallabha Dvivedi (1926–2012) was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He headed the Yogatantra Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and served as Deputy Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–1992).
Vriti Sharma works in the fields of computational studies and Indology. She has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Linguist Vsevolod Bronislavovich Tomashevsky (1891–1927) studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Baudouin de Courtenay and Scherzl. He taught at Baku State University (1920) before serving as Professor of Comparative Linguistics (1924) and Rector (1926–1927) at Saint Petersburg State University.

Vsevolod Miller (1848–1913) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, Indologist, and linguist. He studied at Moscow University under Petrov and Buslaev, subsequently serving there as Docent (1877), as Director of the Lazarev Institute (1897), and Member of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Indologist and philosopher Vsevolod Sergeevič Semencov (1941–1986) studied at Moscow State University's Institute of Asian and African Studies and Banaras Hindu University. He served as naučnyj sotrudnik at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1968–1984) and the Institute of Philosophy (1984).

Linguist and Indologist Vyacheslav Ivanov (1929–2017) studied at Moscow State University under Peterson and Kuznetsov. He held appointments at Moscow State, the Institute of Slavic Studies (~1961–1989), Stanford, Yale, Russian State University for the Humanities, and UCLA (~1992–2015).

Vydūnas (1868–1953) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Königsberg, Greifswald, Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Berlin. He taught Lithuanian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1917–1919) and held a post at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1917–1940).

Linguist and Indologist Václav Machek (1894–1965) earned his Ph.D. at Charles University under Josef Zubatý and studied under Meillet, Bloch, and Lévi in Paris. He was librarian at the Slovakian Library (1921–1924) and became Docent at Masaryk University in 1931.
